The Best Cruiser Riding Gear UK Riders Should Own

The best cruiser riding gear in the UK balances two things that pull in opposite directions: the relaxed, classic style that drew you to a cruiser in the first place, and the honest weather protection you need on an exposed, upright bike in the British climate. A cruiser sits you bolt upright with your chest facing the wind and rain, and unlike a faired tourer there is nothing to hide behind. The gear below embraces the laid-back leather aesthetic while making sure you stay dry, warm and protected when the weather turns, as it always does.

Cruisers are made for savouring the road rather than attacking it, rolling along the A82 beside Loch Lomond or ambling through the Cotswolds on a Sunday. Your kit should match that unhurried spirit while quietly doing its job. For the touring side of cruiser life, our guide on how to tour on a cruiser is a natural companion to this one.

Leather Jackets: Style and Substance

Leather and cruisers go together for good reason. A quality leather jacket looks right on a cruiser, ages beautifully, and offers superb abrasion resistance in a fall. The classic cut suits the upright riding position, and modern cruiser leathers hide CE armour at the shoulders and elbows without spoiling the clean lines.

The Richa Daytona 2 Leather Jacket is a superb example, thick enough to protect yet supple enough to be comfortable from the first ride. The one thing leather does not do is keep the rain out, which is why weather kit further down this list matters so much. For a full comparison, see our roundup of the best leather motorcycle jackets in the UK.

Leather Trousers: Do Not Skip Your Legs

Plenty of cruiser riders pair a good leather jacket with ordinary jeans, which leaves their legs badly exposed. Matching leather trousers complete the look and, more importantly, protect the parts of you most likely to hit the road. Look for a pair with knee and hip armour and a connecting zip to your jacket so there is no gap at the back.

The Furygan Ladakh Leather Trousers offer proper protection with a relaxed cruiser cut that does not feel like race leathers. Our dedicated leather motorcycle trousers guide walks through fit, armour and how to look after them.

The Weather Reality of an Exposed Bike

This is where cruiser riders in Britain must be honest with themselves. Sitting upright with your chest square to the weather, you catch every drop of rain and every gust of wind. Leather offers no waterproofing at all and, once soaked, takes an age to dry and gets uncomfortably cold. The answer is not to abandon leather but to carry a proper waterproof over-layer.

On a cruiser, a packable rain suit is not optional extra kit, it is core equipment. The rider who stuffs one under the seat is the rider still smiling when the heavens open over Glencoe.

A lightweight over-jacket such as the Oxford Rainseal Over Jacket packs down small, pulls straight over your leathers when the sky darkens, and keeps you dry without ruining the look for the ninety per cent of the ride when it is not raining.

Boots: Classic Looks, Real Protection

Cruiser boots lean towards a classic, casual style rather than the technical armour of sports boots, but the good ones still protect the ankle and give a grippy, planted sole for holding a heavy bike at a standstill. A short leather boot with a reinforced toe and heel looks the part on and off the bike.

The Alpinestars Oscar Rayburn Boots nail the retro cruiser look while hiding genuine ankle protection, and they are comfortable enough to walk around in all day when you stop for lunch in a Yorkshire Dales village.

Gloves for the Relaxed Rider

Cruiser gloves favour comfort and classic style, but they still need to protect your palms and knuckles.

  • Warm-weather. A short leather glove such as the Held Rodney Gloves looks right on a cruiser and gives real abrasion resistance.
  • Waterproof pair. Keep an insulated waterproof glove in the luggage for when the weather turns cold and wet.
  • Fit matters. Cruiser bars put your hands out front in the airflow, so a snug glove that seals at the wrist stops cold air funnelling up your sleeve.

Heated Grips and Cold-Weather Comfort

The upright cruiser position leaves your hands hanging out in the wind, so they chill quickly on a cold morning. A set of Oxford Heaterz Cruiser Heated Grips makes early starts and shoulder-season rides genuinely comfortable, and on a big cruiser with plenty of electrical capacity they are an easy fit. Combine them with a windproof layer and you can enjoy the open-road cruiser experience for far more of the year.

Matching Gear to Your Cruiser

How you spec your kit depends on the kind of cruiser miles you do. A rider covering big distances on a bagger like the Harley-Davidson Road Glide will lean hardest on weather protection and heated grips for those long, exposed motorway stretches. Someone enjoying a classic modern retro such as the Triumph Bonneville T120 can go all-in on the timeless leather look for shorter Sunday rides. And a rider on a punchy twin like the Royal Enfield Interceptor 650 gets the best of both, a relaxed cruiser style with enough pace to enjoy a spirited B-road. Whatever you ride, dress for the weather you will actually meet, carry that rain layer, and your cruiser will deliver the unhurried joy it was built for.

faq.q: Do I have to wear leather on a cruiser?
faq.a: No, but leather suits cruisers well. A quality leather jacket looks right, ages beautifully and offers superb abrasion resistance, with modern versions hiding CE armour at the shoulders and elbows. The one thing leather does not do is keep the rain out, so whatever you wear on top, carry a proper waterproof over-layer for the British weather.

faq.q: Why is a rain suit so important on a cruiser?
faq.a: A cruiser sits you bolt upright with your chest facing the wind and rain, and unlike a faired tourer there is nothing to hide behind. Leather offers no waterproofing and, once soaked, takes an age to dry and turns cold. A packable rain suit that lives under the seat and pulls straight over your leathers is core equipment, not an optional extra.

faq.q: Should I wear leather trousers or jeans?
faq.a: Matching leather trousers are strongly recommended. Plenty of cruiser riders pair a good leather jacket with ordinary jeans, which leaves their legs badly exposed in a fall. Choose leather trousers with knee and hip armour and a connecting zip to your jacket so there is no gap at the back. They complete the look and protect the parts most likely to hit the road.

faq.q: What boots work best on a cruiser?
faq.a: Cruiser boots lean towards a classic, casual style rather than technical sports armour, but the good ones still protect the ankle and give a grippy, planted sole for holding a heavy bike at a standstill. A short leather boot with a reinforced toe and heel looks the part and is comfortable enough to walk around in when you stop for lunch.

faq.q: Are heated grips worth it on a cruiser?
faq.a: Very much so. The upright cruiser position leaves your hands hanging out in the wind, so they chill quickly on a cold morning. A big cruiser usually has plenty of electrical capacity to run heated grips, which makes early starts and shoulder-season rides genuinely comfortable. Combine them with a windproof layer and you can enjoy the open road for far more of the year.
